analysis.title: Silver: The great washout
key_insights: Silver trades 25% below its 200-day moving average, the widest discount since the March 2020 Covid liquidation. Before that, a comparable dislocation requires going back to 2013.
Speculative positioning has been flushed. Per JPM, managed money net length is at its lowest since Q1 2024.

Solar demand for silver is expected to fall roughly 30%, about 60 million ounces, this year, with weakness extending into 2027. Per JPM, this is a significant shift for a market used to structural deficits.
The risk is that silver is moving toward surplus just as speculative positioning gets washed out.
A stronger dollar has coincided with weaker silver all year.
Silver is testing its 100-week moving average. The longer-term trendline sits lower, around $48, and is flagged as a key technical area.
The note argues extreme oversold conditions alone will not fix a deteriorating fundamental backdrop, and that oversold can persist longer than traders expect.
risk_factors: Stronger dollar continues to weigh on silver.
Solar demand for silver expected to fall about 30% (roughly 60 million ounces) this year, with weakness into 2027.
Silver may be shifting from structural deficit toward surplus.
Oversold conditions can persist, so a technical washout may not mark a bottom.

tension_points.bull_case: Silver is at its deepest discount to the 200-day moving average since March 2020 and speculative longs have disappeared, which is the kind of exhaustion selling that can precede a bounce.
